crop_note: sheet fills frame; corners slightly trimmed/rounded
evidence: Title 'Sunrise' (日之出) plus pink clouds at the horizon and a departing daimyo procession = dawn; clear sky with streaky cloud. No plants, festival or clothing cue for season.
taxonomy_friction: No season cue at all; I used null for season, but the brief frames null as 'no meaningful answer' rather than 'unknown', and these are different things (an outdoor scene does have a season, we just can't tell). Procession is a genre cue (figures) but the town/sea setting dominates.

crop_note: sheet fills frame; corners trimmed, slight foxing
evidence: Even daylight, pale sky, slight haze over distant fields. Traveller dismounting at the Komeya inn = arrival, so a dusk share per the activity rule, but light is plain day; time partly a guess. No season cue.
taxonomy_friction: Activity convention (arriving at inn = dusk) contradicts the visual light; the rule doesn't say which wins. Red band at top of sky (bokashi) is the red variant of ichimonji-bokashi, not covered explicitly by the convention notes.

crop_note: narrow sheet margin left/right; no backdrop
evidence: Cherry trees in full bloom with blossom-viewers on the hill = spring (title date 4th month 1856). Clear pale sky; red glow at the horizon may be bokashi convention or dusk, so time partly a guess.
taxonomy_friction: Red/pink horizon gradation is as common as the blue ichimonji-bokashi and is ambiguous between convention and dusk glow; the notes only cover the blue top band. Gotenyama was a quarried hill: 'hilly' vs. the stream-plain foreground is a split I had to invent.

place.name: Lake Kawaguchi from Misaka pass road (Kai Province)

crop_note: sheet fills frame with uninked paper margin around image; vertical centre fold/join line
evidence: Clear sky with red top band and a faint pink horizon (likely convention). Fuji is shown snowless and trees are green, so summer leaning; the famous winter reflection is faded in this impression. Time mostly a guess.
taxonomy_friction: Snowless Fuji is an important season cue that isn't in the marker list (snow-capped vs. bare Fuji). The print plays two seasons at once (summer peak, winter reflection) which a single season vector can only smear. Red ichimonji-bokashi not covered by the convention note.

crop_note: image trimmed close to the image border; minimal margin at right
evidence: Clear sky, calm sea with modest surf. Orange horizon under a dark top band is probably convention; time split because neither title nor activity gives a clue. No season cue.
taxonomy_friction: Fuji drawn on the horizon from Chōshi is a pictorial liberty; the 'fuji' flag can't distinguish real view from artistic insertion. Mixed beach + rocky headland terrain needed a flat/hilly split. Moderate breakers but no wind indication: wind and sea state are conflated in the wind definition ('whipped-up waves').

crop_note: sheet nearly fills frame; small loss top-right corner, slight discoloration
evidence: Title '(Reflection of Moon)'; moon shown only as reflection in water, red streak in pale sky = dusk/night. Flowering bush clover (hagi) = autumn grasses / moon viewing.
taxonomy_friction: Moon appears only as a reflection; the moon flag doesn't distinguish this. Court figures are large (borderline for 'setting dominates'). Water type unidentifiable (pond or river). Sky is pale/unprinted despite night: night shown by subject not palette.

crop_note: sheet on a lighter backdrop; deckle/torn top edge; wide margins with pencil title and signature
evidence: Title 'Evening in Nara' (奈良の夕); lit hanging lanterns, blue-teal twilight sky and silhouetted cryptomeria = dusk into night. No season cue.
taxonomy_friction: Shin-hanga uses naturalistic light, so the ukiyo-e conventions don't apply in the same way; genre is architecture-dominant, which none of the four genres names (I used landscape). Temple veranda view: settlement category (temple precinct in a town park) fits poorly.

crop_note: sheet fills frame with paper margin; small stain top-right
evidence: Pale grey-white sky under a red top band; even light = day. A man wading barefoot to wash a horse and lush green reeds suggest the warm season, weakly.
taxonomy_friction: Pale/unprinted sky is ambiguous between clear and overcast; the clear vs. cloudy distinction is often unreadable in prints with no sky colour. Okazaki Castle visible: no flag for castles.

crop_note: sheet fills frame; corners trimmed
evidence: Still life of red snapper and halfbeak on a plain teal ground; no sky, setting or seasonal plant.
taxonomy_friction: Fish still lifes are filed under bird_and_flower but have no weather, time or environment; nearly all dimensions null, so it will score neutral everywhere. Fish do have seasons (sayori is a spring fish) but no marker exists for food/fish seasonality.

crop_note: sheet fills frame; wide cream margin around the light-blue image area
evidence: Flatfish, abalone and loquat fruit (biwa) on plain ground; loquats ripen in early summer (June). No sky or setting.
taxonomy_friction: New marker 'loquat' (biwa fruit, peak ~10 June) needed. Same still-life issue as fish prints: all scene dimensions null.

exclude_reason: brush sketch/drawing (sketch sheet), not a finished print
crop_note: small square sheet inside a passe-partout mat; mat fills outer frame
evidence: Grey brush sketch of a boat with a figure (or grass) on a tiny square sheet; no scene to tag.
taxonomy_friction: Drawings/sketch sheets in the sample aren't prints at all; exclusion list mentions sketchbooks but not single drawings.

crop_note: narrow margin strip at left edge (sheet edge/joining edge); likely one sheet of a triptych
evidence: Flocks of wild geese crossing the sky and descending over the sea = autumn; grey cloud band but bright light, day. Choppy waves and surf suggest some wind.
taxonomy_friction: Likely one sheet of a 'Fūryū Genji' triptych; this sheet alone is a pure landscape, so I included it, but the brief excludes triptychs and doesn't say how to treat a single sheet. Geese here are flying, not specifically descending (marker says 'descending').

crop_note: later reproduction on a card with printed English caption below the image
evidence: Rice sheaves stacked in harvested paddies and farmers at work = autumn harvest; mountains fading in grey haze. Daylight activity; time not explicit.
taxonomy_friction: New marker 'rice_harvest' (sheaves/inaba, peak ~1 Oct) needed. This is a later reproduction ('after Hiroshige', English caption); no field for reproduction/later edition. Hazy grey sky could be mist, overcast or just a muted reprint palette.

crop_note: sheet fills frame; mount/tape strip along top edge
evidence: Dark grey sky, full moon over the water and its reflection = night (subject: Abe no Nakamaro gazing at the moon). No seasonal cue.
taxonomy_friction: Setting is legendary China (Mingzhou), not locatable; place null. Moon strongly evokes autumn tsukimi by convention but the poem has no season, so I left season null. Figures are prominent; 'setting dominates' is borderline for poem-picture series.

exclude_reason: surimono still life (ceremonial objects), no scene
crop_note: sheet fills frame; small collector's/inventory marks lower left
evidence: Tide jewels and sickle on a plum-patterned cloth over a table; no landscape, sky or setting.
taxonomy_friction: Plum blossom appears only as a textile pattern; unclear whether decorative motifs should count as seasonal markers (I did not). Surimono are often New Year pieces, which would be a season cue the schema can't capture without a visible marker.

crop_note: sheet fills frame; small tears/losses along left edge and corners
evidence: Grey mountains fading towards their bases = atmospheric haze; full sails = some wind; even daylight. No season cue.
taxonomy_friction: Lake Hamana is a brackish lagoon open to the sea: lake vs. sea split was arbitrary. Grey gradation on mountains is half convention, half haze; hard to apply the suyari-gasumi rule to tonal (not banded) mist.

crop_note: sheet fills frame with paper margin; light staining
evidence: Peach trees in bloom and yellow rapeseed/wildflowers = spring; clear blue sky with ichimonji-bokashi; daytime travellers. Time from daylight activity, no title cue.
taxonomy_friction: New marker 'peach_blossom' (momo, peak ~5 Apr) needed: distinct from plum and cherry and common in prints. Rapeseed (nanohana, ~late Mar) is another candidate marker.

crop_note: sheet nearly fills frame; slight soiling top-left
evidence: Snow lying on fence and ground with flowering plum = late winter; hand lantern suggests night, but the ground is flat green (stage convention); time a guess.
taxonomy_friction: Stage/theatrical settings: snow and lantern are props, not real conditions. Fine for excluded prints but it shows the schema can't mark a 'theatrical' setting.

crop_note: sheet fills frame; paper loss along top-left edge
evidence: Snow lying on pines and ground, girls building a snow dog = winter. Yellow ground is Harunobu's decorative background, not dusk; time a guess. Torii at the shrine.
taxonomy_friction: Flat coloured grounds (yellow, grey) carry no time-of-day meaning; worth adding to the convention notes. Maple-leaf kimono pattern is clothing decoration, not an autumn marker, though the notes say clothing can indicate season.

exclude_reason: surimono showing a mechanical puppet (karakuri) stage display, not a real scene
crop_note: sheet fills frame
evidence: Pictured tableau (shrine torii, arched bridge, pines, boats) on a stage platform; no real sky or time cues, defaults only.
taxonomy_friction: A surimono with a scene, but the scene is a depicted stage display; the brief's 'surimono with no scene' rule doesn't cover depicted artifice.
